newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended broadly lower in scant dealings Friday, as speculative long liquidation pressured the market, trading sources said.
After rallying some $40 a tonne in the last two sessions, prices gapped $10 lower at the outset on the heels of a weak performance overnight in the London cocoa market.
"The specs who bought over the past couple of days bailed out," one dealer said.
The most-active March contract breached near-term chart support at around $1,378 a tonne, sinking to a low of $1,374, just shy of the next support level at $1,372, dealers said.
Steady trade buying toward the lows helped to offset selling pressure from speculators, they added.
March delivery ended $11 a tonne lower, at $1,382, after ranging between $1,387 and $1,374. Second-month May also fell $11, to close at $1,404, while the back months finished down $11 to $12.
Turnover was thin, at an estimated 4,193 lots.
After the $1,372 mark, traders pegged March's next support level at $1,366-$1,362. To the upside, resistance was seen at Thursday's high of $1,395, then around $1,404-$1,408.
Traders await the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders Report, anticipating the figures will show an increase in non-commercial short positions.

The biweekly report for the weeks ended December 24 and December 31 will be issued on Monday, January 6, after 1530 EST (2030 GMT) -- a one day delay due to this week's New Year's holiday, the CFTC said.

Market participants also look forward to European and U.S. fourth quarter cocoa grind data for fresh fundamental impetus. The figures are slated for release over the next two weeks. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
